ns2:section.sectionText: Section Title: Acting Out Algorithms (Systems and Networking) Computer networks are pretty confusing. They use a variety of complicated distributed algorithms (routing protocols, transport protocols, cryptographic techniques and authentication mechanisms,commit/election/agreement protocols, DHTs, etc) that are hard to understand. In this seminar class we build an in-depth understanding of these protocols by physically acting out their operations. Students take the role of "packet" or "routers" or "files" and walk around to carry information. We use props to make things more clear: a student's "IP address" is written on a name tag ("hi, my name is 10.1.7.25"), we use pieces of paper for packets and write on envelopes to represent packet headers, and students exchange whiteboard signs to advertise information and delegate authority. A set of 2-4 students are given the role of directors to design these human-based algorithms and make everything run smoothly. The goal of this course is to make learning about complex concepts "fun" and enjoyable, to "break the ice" to encourage discussion and asking of questions, to force us all to gain a complete and deep understanding of protocols by grappling with tricky issues in protocols that become apparent when designing a real implementation, to work with their peers to make sure everyone understands the algorithm (often necessary for the exercise to "work"), and to get the chance to practice speaking and communication of complex concepts in an easygoing and accepting environment.
